title: All things work together (Romans 8:28)
hook: to them that love God all things work together unto good

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Spirit praying in us with sighs too deep for words. Your line was the spirit prays for us. Did a sigh become a prayer? Day five hundred sixty-six.

It's printed on mugs and greeting cards. People say it at funerals, sometimes kindly, sometimes too fast. Everything happens for a reason. It's usually meant well. And on a terrible day, it can land like a slap. Some who say it think they're quoting the Bible. So it's worth looking carefully at the verse it's often borrowed from, because what Paul actually says is both stronger and more careful than the greeting card.
screen: `ON MUGS AND GREETING CARDS.` → `EVERYTHING HAPPENS FOR A REASON?` → `WHAT PAUL ACTUALLY SAYS.`

segments.voice: Here's the verse, in the Douay-Rheims: "And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints." Notice first what it doesn't say. It doesn't say all things are good. Paul has just been talking about groaning, suffering, and a creation in labor pains. In the next verses he'll list tribulation, famine, the sword. He knows terrible things are terrible. Second, notice the verb: work together. The Greek is sunergei, works together. Not each thing is good on its own, but all things, woven together, are made to serve good. Third, notice who's doing the weaving. Paul's point is that the good isn't automatic, like fate. It comes from someone: the God whose Spirit, Paul said two verses earlier, prays in us. And fourth, the good Paul means is bigger than comfort. The next verse says it plainly: to be conformed to the image of his Son. Becoming like Christ. Paul doesn't offer the verse as an explanation of why the bad thing happened. And he never says the reason will be visible. He says, we know.
screen: `NOT: ALL THINGS ARE GOOD.` · `SUNERGEI: WORKING TOGETHER.` · `GOD IS THE ONE WHO WEAVES.` · `THE GOOD: BECOMING LIKE CHRIST.` · then, large: `ALL THINGS WORK TOGETHER UNTO GOOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look for good in a setback. Gently. Settle, and breathe. Choose a setback from your past, not your deepest wound, just something that went wrong. A job you didn't get. A move you didn't want. A plan that fell apart. Look at it from here. Was anything woven out of it, a friendship, a strength, a patience, a direction you wouldn't have found? If you find something, let yourself be grateful. If you don't, that's honest too; Paul says we know, not that we see. If you pray, you can hand God what you can't make sense of yet. The bell holds the time.
All things work together. Paul's claim: not that everything is good, but that God weaves all things, even the hard ones, toward good for those who love him. Today's word.
Your line: all things. Today, when something goes wrong, skip the greeting card, and just ask what might be woven from it. Day five hundred sixty-six.

howItsDone: Catholics speak of divine providence, God's care that guides all things toward good without causing evil, and some offer up their sufferings, uniting them with Christ's, trusting God to bring good from them.

myth: Romans 8:28 says that all things are good
it says all things work together for good. Paul knows hard things are hard.
Paul says we know all things work together, not that we will see how
the verse says we know. it never promises the reason will be visible.
the good Paul means is mainly comfort
the next verse names it: being conformed to the image of his Son.

fork.setup: a grieving friend is told everything happens for a reason. you're asked what Romans 8:28 really says. what do you say?
options: that God caused this for a reason.
that God works even in this toward good, though we may not see how.
that it isn't really so bad.
fork.reveal: the verse doesn't call the bad thing good. it says God works all things together toward good for those who love him.

trapdoor: what you thought: everything happens for a reason.
what it means: not that all things are good, but that God weaves all things, even suffering, toward good for those who love him.
what a scholar hears: sunergei answers the Spirit's help two verses earlier, and the good is defined in the next verse: being made conformable to the image of the Son.

notes: Confirm KJV wording of Romans 8:28 and the Douay-Rheims phrase 'to them that love God, all things work together unto good'.
Manuscripts reading 'ho theos' (P46, Alexandrinus, Vaticanus): confirm.
CCC 313 cites Romans 8:28 on providence; confirm.
The practice deliberately avoids asking listeners to revisit their deepest wounds.
